params.body:
## Why

Since 19 November 2026 the source links in the designed reports lead through Gentells: each one opens `gentells.com/sources/<key>`. The site is still behind the launch cover, so a reader of a report who has no preview link and no account lands on the holding page instead of the source. The reports go to a wider group on 20 November.

## What

`sources/*` joins the paths the cover always lets through (`PreLaunch::ALWAYS_OPEN`).

- A source page shows the publisher, the title, the date, where Gentells cites it and the way out to the publisher. It carries `noindex, follow` already.
- What it links on to (a trend, a post, a report) stays behind the cover: a reader without a link meets the holding page there, as before.
- A key that names no source is still a 404.

To weigh: the page names the reports and posts that cite the source and the public trends it feeds, by title. Those titles become readable before launch for anyone who holds a source link.

## Checked

- `PreLaunchTest`: a new case opens a source page through the cover, keeps the noindex, answers 404 for an unknown key, and shows `/trends` and `/reports` still covered. 19/19.
- Full suite 666 of 667 locally; the one failure is `BuildStampTest`, which reads the checkout's git folder and does not find one in a worktree. Pint clean on the touched files.
params.title: A source a report cites opens through the launch cover
